metadata.description: Single-plugin marketplace exposing the cc-enforcer discipline plugin.

plugins.name: cc-enforcer
plugins.description: Rules your coding agent physically cannot ignore. A Claude Code plugin (and LLM-agnostic rule pack) that stops reactive patching, guessed citations, surface-level fixes and premature "done" claims by intercepting the agent's own tool calls rather than asking it nicely. PreToolUse denies an edit before it lands — editing a file you never opened this session, a suppression marker with no adjacent why-comment, a hardcoded secret or user-home path, the fourth small patch to one file, a dangerous shell flag. A nine-layer Stop gate then refuses to let a completion claim end the turn without evidence, a convergence self-quiz, a fidelity check against the user's ORIGINAL request, and a one-line TL;DR. Twelve rules, eight backed by a hook; "Imperial Edict" regexes you define per project; a repo-wide sync gate; three CI drift gates that derive every documented number from the code so the documentation cannot rot. Zero dependencies, stdlib only, Linux + Windows CI, and every guard fails OPEN — a bug in the discipline can never brick your agent. v0.34.0 adds env-file hygiene: Claude Code sources CLAUDE_ENV_FILE into every Bash call, SessionStart fires on every compact/resume, and a plugin that appends its exports unconditionally on that event grows the file without bound — a real session lost every Bash call silently at ~8 KB of duplicates. The true origin (a third-party plugin's non-idempotent append) is out of reach, but the class is this plugin's remit: lib/envfile.py now dedupes the file on every SessionStart, keeping the last occurrence per variable — byte-equivalent to what sourcing already yields, so nothing observable changes, only the growth goes. Refusal over gamble: any shape the line model does not represent (non-export lines, a quoted value spanning lines) refuses the whole pass byte-identically, each acceptance case shipping with its refusal twin. 604 -> 615 tests. Prior — v0.33.0 renames the project: cc-enslaver is now cc-enforcer. Same twelve rules, same hooks, a name that says what the thing does. Everything derived from the name moves with it: the /cc-enforcer:* command namespace, the CC_ENFORCER_* environment variables, the per-project config directory .claude/cc-enforcer/{edicts,sync-gate}.toml, the install coordinate cc-enforcer@cc-enforcer, and the GitHub URL (the old one redirects). BREAKING for existing installs, deliberately without a compat shim: both config loaders are failing-open, so an unmigrated .claude/cc-enslaver/ directory does not error — it silently stops enforcing, which is exactly why the migration is one loud directory rename instead of a quiet fallback that would leave two truth locations forever. The rename also caught the defect class a rename is built to catch: two CLI sites composed the config path from their own copy of the plugin-name literal instead of the shared constant. manage_edicts --global would have WRITTEN to the old directory while the loader READ the new one, and sync-gate's path command printed a would-be location derived from the process cwd that add (which honours CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR) would never write to — the same print-vs-write divergence class as v0.31's birth defect, one command over. Both are now single definitions (lib/edicts gained a public global_path(); cmd_path prints through the deterministic write resolver), each pinned by a regression test plus the twin that keeps equality from being satisfied by two identical literals. CHANGELOG history is NOT rewritten: past entries keep the name the project shipped under, because a dated record claiming /cc-enforcer:gc existed in v0.6.1 would be a lie with a version number on it. 601 -> 604 tests. Prior — v0.32.2 answers "are all the docs updated?" by checking instead of asserting, and found two that were not. No code change. The audit that matters is the COMPLEMENT: diff the markdown touched across the release series against every markdown in the repo, then read the UNTOUCHED files for claims the releases invalidated. Both defects were in that set; neither was reachable from "did I update the README" — the README was fine. FIRST, a cross-document claim true in only one direction: commands/sync-gate.md (added v0.31.0) told the reader that the repo-refresh skill should call its `add` and close with `check`, while the skill's own Step 6 still said hand-edit the TOML, with no mention of the CLI that had existed for two releases and none of `check`. Document A asserted that document B does X; document B did not know — drift introduced by documenting a new coupling on one side only. Step 6 now carries the invocation, states that `check` is the step's convergence check rather than an optional extra (the loader is failing-open: a mistyped glob never fires and never complains), and repeats that groups are asserted by a human, never guessed. ARCHITECTURE section 8 gains the coupling as a row with the lesson: a cross-document claim IS a coupling and must be verified from BOTH ends. SECOND, docs/RULES.md’s rule-to-component table listed only lib/sync_gate.py for rule 12, so the CLI and slash command that manage its config were missing from the one table whose job is that mapping. No new gate was added for it, deliberately: test_doc_sync derives every pinned fact from the CODE, while this table maps a judgement no derivation can produce, and a gate over it would compare one hand-maintained list against another — the doc-to-doc comparison that file’s own design notes forbid. Recorded as a known uncovered surface instead of papered over with coverage-shaped decoration. 601 tests unchanged. Prior — v0.32.1 closes the project out: the roadmap is retired and the rule text catches up with what the code enforces. No behaviour change. The one that mattered: `rules/` is not internal documentation, it is the LLM-AGNOSTIC PRODUCT — `cat rules/*.md` is a documented install path for agents that do not speak Claude Code's plugin protocol — and rules/12 still described the v0.27 escape hatch after v0.32 tightened it, so a rule-pack consumer was told the hatch was looser than the hook actually is. Same class as v0.26's docstring claiming nesting was handled, one layer out; fixed in the English skeleton, the zh mirror, and commands/checklist.md at the point of use. The roadmap is now empty by decision, with both remaining entries retired in all THREE places they were listed (the third, docs/EDICTS.md, would have been missed by anyone editing only the first two): per-session ephemeral edicts are DROPPED, structurally rather than for effort — the edict CLI is a Bash subprocess with no session_id, only a hook payload carries one, which is why register_read's authoritative half lives in bash_guard — and the layer-(g) content-hash upgrade is RETIRED with its premise measured false: it assumed 1-second mtime granularity, while consecutive writes on this plugin's primary platform are distinguishable at 1 ms and layer (g) compares a first-encounter baseline against closing time, seconds apart, three orders of magnitude clear of the collision window. Reopen on a reproduction, not a hypothesis. 601 tests unchanged. Prior — v0.32.0 closes the two items v0.31 recorded instead of fixing, both decided by the user. FIRST, Stop layer (i) now rejects a sync acknowledgement that answers nothing: `_has_sync_marker` was presence-only, so `sync-check: n/a` — and a marker the agent merely QUOTED — settled a named co-update group as firmly as a real sweep report. It now applies the two tests layer (h) already applies to `tldr`, through the same lib/mdctx model: attribution (a marker inside a non-canonical fence or a blockquote is illustrative, not a claim) and substance (the value must carry content, on its own line or the next non-blank one; a bare placeholder is treated as absent, and a non-answer cannot borrow the following line). The limit is pinned by its own test so it cannot drift into an implied guarantee: vacuous PROSE (`sync-check: checked it`) is still accepted and is not claimed to be detected, because refusing an honest report is the worse error. A deliberate strictness increase. SECOND, `check` now runs against this repository in CI. v0.31.0 shipped it arguing that an unenforced gate you still trust is worse than none, and gave it a non-zero exit specifically so it could run in CI — then never ran it on itself, the same defect one level up. Wired as a test rather than a workflow step, matching test_i18n_sync, so a local unittest run covers it too, and shipped with the twin that keeps a green check from meaning an empty config. 594 -> 601 tests. Prior — v0.31.1 folds rule 12's acknowledgement into the reply schema. Every other closing obligation (before / edits / convergence / fidelity / closing / tldr) has been a schema FIELD since v0.20, whose design is that the field name IS the Stop-hook marker; rule 12 arrived three releases later and its sync acknowledgement stayed free prose with no slot to write it in — the only duty whose omission looked like an ordinary reply. It is now `sync-check:` (zh: `同步核对:`) in all four injected prompts. Zero hook code changed: the key already matches SYNC_MARKERS. It does NOT weaken layer (i), verified by probe rather than by reading — since v0.27 a marker settles only groups a previous block actually NAMED, so a first violation still blocks and names its group, and the field is where the answer to that group goes next turn. A vacuous `sync-check: n/a` still settles a named group; that is unchanged from today's free-prose markers, is called out in both prompts, and adding a substance check would be a strictness contract change deliberately not made here. The release also found a pre-existing drift: README.zh.md's version badge said 0.29.0 at 0.31.1 — two releases stale with every gate green — because the badge check pinned README.md and not its mirror; it now discovers every README*.md from disk. 590 -> 594 tests. Prior — v0.31.0 made the rule-12 sync gate INSPECTABLE. Its co-update groups have been enforceable since v0.23 and authorable only by hand-writing TOML, with no way to see what the loader made of it — and that loader is failing-open by design, so a dropped group or a glob matching no file does not raise; it simply stops guarding, printing one stderr line nobody reads. An unenforced gate you still trust is worse than no gate, because you have stopped looking at it. The new `/cc-enforcer:sync-gate` command (init / list / check / add / remove / path) closes the hole: `check` reports every group the loader kept, every group it DROPPED and why, and every glob matching no file in the repo, exiting 1 so it can run in CI. Deliberately NOT auto-created: no hook writes into the user's project directory — an invariant that has held for every release — and an auto-created empty template would be functionally identical to no file at all (zero groups means Stop layer (i) stays inert), bought at the price of an unrequested file in everyone's git status. Writes are verified twice, not once: not merely "does this parse" but "does the loader still keep every group", because a `require = []` entry is perfectly valid TOML that sync_gate.load() silently discards — a parse-only check would let the CLI report success over a group that guards nothing. On failure the previous file is restored byte-for-byte. One defect found during this feature's own first smoke test is reported here rather than quietly fixed: the CLI chose its write target with config_path(), the resolver built for READING, which tries several candidate roots and takes the first that already holds a file — so a run targeting a project with no config yet fell through to the process cwd and appended two groups to this plugin's own config. The root cause is that "where do I read from" and "where do I write to" are different questions, and a read-resolver's fallback chain is precisely what makes it the wrong answer to the second. Fixed at the mechanism (default_project_path, deterministic; load_file, no fallback), swept across both call sites, and the read resolver's fallback is now pinned by its own test so a later "make them both deterministic" cannot silently break the hook path. Also, lib/tomlio.py now owns the TOML writer alongside the reader, so the edict CLI and the sync-gate CLI share one encoder rather than letting the second copy miss the next fix. 565 → 590 tests. Prior — v0.30.0 was a structural audit of the plugin itself, on one theme: a thing that is written down is not a thing that is enforced. Seven unreachable production symbols were deleted rather than annotated, among them a retired rationale checker left standing beside the live one — where the next reader has no way to tell which of the two the guard actually consults — and an `_escape_triple_quoted` marked "kept only so an external caller does not break" that no caller could reach. Three duplicated judgements were collapsed to one definition each: markdown fence parsing existed in three copies, each carrying its own transcription of the same v0.25 CommonMark fix, and the project-root predicate existed twice with the second annotated "same project-root heuristic as lib/edicts.py" — a comment that names an invariant without holding it, so widening one copy silently leaves the other behind (new shared module: lib/projroot.py). And the Stop status table stopped making a claim of its own kind: layers are DISPLAYED (a) through (i) but EVALUATED with (b) first, because a hedge invalidates a done-claim however much evidence sits beside it — yet the table derived both "Pass" and "pending" from the display index, so every hedge block printed "(a) PASS", asserting that convergence evidence had been found on a turn where `_has_evidence` was never called. A gate built to catch unfounded claims does not get to make one; fixed, with twin tests in both directions. The file tree was reclassified rather than rearranged: test files are named for what they cover and indexed file-by-file in tests/README.md, hooks/scripts/ labels its three roles inline, and docs/ gained an index. The four non-hook scripts deliberately did NOT move into a tools/ directory — gc_state.py is imported by inject_context.py for auto-GC and register_read.py's real logic lives inside bash_guard.py, so neither is a standalone CLI and the move would trade a tidier directory name for a real cross-tree sys.path splice. CLAUDE.md shrank from 87 KB to 39 KB: its "current version" section had grown into a verbatim second copy of the changelog, re-read into context on every single session and free to drift from the original. 564 → 565 tests, all green on Linux and Windows. Full release history lives in CHANGELOG.md, which is now its only copy.
